what: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Import, score, analyse ScoreMe questionnaire data R.  [!WARNING] tallieR early development formally tested. API may change without notice, scoring algorithms validated reference implementations, package undergone peer review. Use caution verify outputs independently using research context.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: tallieR official R companion ScoreMe app. study session ends, ScoreMe exports participant data single JSON file. tallieR reads file — whole directory exports — re-scores every questionnaire raw item-level responses using algorithms embedded app, hands tidy data frames ready downstream analysis. covers 27 validated instruments across five clinical domains: sleep, mental health, wellbeing, physical activity, neurodevelopmental screening. Custom instruments defined ScoreMe-compatible JSON files can loaded scored API, without modifying package. tallieR designed work alongside slumbR: ScoreMe handles questionnaire side study, Sleep Diaries handles diary side, two R packages bring data streams together R.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: 📥 read_scoreme() — parse ScoreMe JSON export structured tallier_export object 📂 read_scoreme_dir() — batch-read whole directory exports tallier_study 📊 scores_wide() — one row per participant, one column per questionnaire (recent session) 📋 scores_long() — one row per participant × questionnaire × administration (full history retained) 🔬 items_long() — one row per item response, factor analysis, IRT, reliability checks 🧮 score_questionnaire() — re-score built-instrument raw answers list 💬 interpret_score() — return clinical score band (label, colour, description) score 📋 available_instruments() — list supported questionnaires IDs, domains, beta status 📁 load_instrument() — compile custom questionnaire ScoreMe JSON spec 📁 load_instrument_dir() — batch-load directory custom instrument specs 📐 cronbach_alpha() — compute Cronbach’s α exact 95% CIs questionnaire data

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Note PSQI: score_questionnaire("psqi", answers) returns named list global seven component scores (C1–C7). Use result$global total. Note MCTQ: score_questionnaire("mctq", answers) returns named list: msfsc (corrected mid-sleep free days, decimal hours), sjl (social jetlag, hours), plus msw, msf, sd_w, sd_f. Expected answer keys: bt_w, sl_w, wt_w, bt_f, sl_f, wt_f (times {hour, minute} lists decimal hours; latencies numeric minutes), wd (workdays per week).

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Note DASS-21: returns named list total, depression, anxiety, stress subscale scores (scaled × 2 align DASS-42 norms). Note PANSS: returns named list total, positive, negative, general subscale scores.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: Note WHOQOL-BREF: returns named list total four domain scores (physical, psychological, social, environment), scaled 0–100.

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: tallieR can score questionnaires built package, long defined ScoreMe-compatible JSON spec. allows study-specific proprietary instruments flow pipeline without modifying tallieR source code. Supported scoring types compiled JSON spec: "sum", "weighted_sum", "mean". Instruments "composite" scoring (e.g. PSQI-style multi-component algorithms) can loaded return NA scoring; can override compiled score function assigning custom one loading: See vignette("custom-instruments", package = "tallieR") system.file("extdata", "example_instrument.json", package = "tallieR") full JSON spec schema.
code: # Load a single custom instrument my_instr <- load_instrument("path/to/fss.json")  # Score it with the standard API score_questionnaire("fss", answers, instruments = my_instr)  # Load a whole directory of specs custom <- load_instrument_dir("instruments/")  # Use with read_scoreme() so custom instruments are scored on import exp  <- read_scoreme("export.json", instruments = custom) wide <- scores_wide(exp) my_instr$my_id$score <- function(answers) { ... }

title: tallieR — R tools for ScoreMe questionnaire data
text: cronbach_alpha() computes Cronbach’s α exact 95% confidence intervals (Feldt et al., 1987) questionnaire present data. Non-numeric items (MCTQ clock times, STOP-BANG yes/) silently dropped estimation. function accepts either tallier_export/tallier_study object data frame returned items_long().
code: study <- read_scoreme_dir("exports/")  # All questionnaires cronbach_alpha(study) #>  questionnaire_id alpha ci_lower ci_upper n_items n_obs note #>               ess  0.87     0.82     0.91       8    48   NA #>               isi  0.91     0.87     0.94       7    48   NA #>               phq9 0.85     0.80     0.90       9    42   NA #>  ...  # Specific subset cronbach_alpha(study, questionnaires = c("ess", "isi", "phq9"))  # From an items_long() data frame (e.g. after filtering) items <- items_long(study) cronbach_alpha(items)

what: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
text: Computes Cronbach's alpha (measure internal consistency) questionnaire present tallier_export tallier_study object. Item-level responses extracted via items_long(), coerced numeric, participant × item matrix constructed per questionnaire.

title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
code: cronbach_alpha(obj, questionnaires = NULL, conf_level = 0.95, min_items = 2L)

title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
text: obj tallier_export tallier_study object, data frame returned items_long() (must contain columns participant_id, questionnaire_id, item_id, completed_at, response). questionnaires Character vector questionnaire IDs include. Defaults questionnaires present obj. conf_level Numeric. Confidence level CI (default 0.95). Uses exact F-distribution method Feldt et al. (1987). min_items Integer. Minimum number numeric items required attempt estimation (default 2).

title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
text: data.frame one row per questionnaire columns: questionnaire_id Questionnaire identifier. alpha Cronbach's alpha (standardised scale: −∞ 1). ci_lower Lower bound conf_level CI. ci_upper Upper bound conf_level CI. n_items Number numeric items used. n_obs Number complete observations (participants). note NA success, short message explaining estimation failed.

title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha
text: Non-numeric items (e.g. MCTQ clock times, STOP-BANG yes/) silently dropped estimation. Questionnaires fewer 2 numeric items fewer 2 complete observations return NA explanatory note.

title: Cronbach's alpha for one or more questionnaires — cronbach_alpha

Statistical inference coefficient alpha. Applied Psychological Measurement, 11(1), 93–103. doi:10.1177/014662168701100107
